patches.name: 0209--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-hid-asus-ally-Separate-trigger-rumble-from-main-rumble.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] hid-asus-ally: Separate trigger rumble
 from main rumble
patches.rationale:
The driver copies main rumble values into additional rumble fields, which
are now used for trigger rumble on the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X. This causes
both the main rumble and the new trigger rumble motors to fire at the
same intensity on ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X, which effectively double rumble
intensity on that model.

This is already a no-op on older Ally models that do not have trigger
rumble and we don't use the trigger rumble for anything on SteamOS, so
we can just disable it by separating out the trigger rumble fields.

patches.name: 0210--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-fbdev-client-Don-t-enable-fbdev-emulation-for-virtio-gpu-driver.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/fbdev-client: Don't enable fbdev
 emulation for virtio-gpu driver
patches.rationale:
VirtIO-GPU driver has a known problem with fbdev emulation + native context
where guest Xorg would create framebuffer from a dumb (vrend) BO before
native context has been set up for the Xorg's DRM context. This results in
a corrupted rendering when that dumb BO is further used from within native
context, which rejects it and skips rendering. Problem affects only Xorg and
not presents with Wayland. The fix primary wanted for SDDM and other DMs that
use Xorg.

patches.name: 0220--FOR-UPSTREAM-Expose-control-over-the-boot-animation-color..patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] Expose control over the boot animation color.
patches.rationale:
Adds a new sysfs node called `multi_intensity_startup`, which allows for setting the intensity of the RGB LED components at startup of the device. This allows for controlling the color of the startup animation.

Values written to `multi_intensity_startup` persist across power cycles, and are expected to be in the same format as values written to `multi_intensity`, i.e. three space-separated integer values in the range 0-255 representing the R, G, and B components of the color.

patches.name: 0221--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-ACPI-PM-s2idle-Add-lps0_screen_off-sysfs-interface.patch

subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] ACPI: PM: s2idle: Add lps0_screen_off
 sysfs interface
patches.rationale:
Add `/sys/power/lps0_screen_off` interface to allow userspace to control
Display OFF/ON DSM notifications at runtime. Writing "1" to this file
triggers the OFF notification, and "0" triggers the ON notification.

Userspace should write "1" after turning off all physical and remote
displays. It should write "0" before turning on any of displays.

patches.name: 0224--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Refactor-and-clean-up-report-parsing.patch

subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Refactor and clean up report
 parsing
patches.rationale:
This switches from a parsing style where each button or axis is parsed
individually out of a report using !!(byte & BIT(x)) style. This commit
switches it to a mostly unified approach of defining a list of individual
mappings in an array and passing it to a function that handles all of the
extraction. Theoretically this is more lines, but in practice it results in
(subjectively) cleaner code. Some exceptions still need to be made for
things like handling the lizard mode toggle key, but in general there's a
lot less manual code.

patches.rationale:

patches.name: 0228--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Fully-unregister-controller-when-hidraw-is-opened.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Fully unregister controller when
 hidraw is opened
patches.rationale:
To avoid conflicts between anything touching the hidraw and the driver we
had previously detached the evdev nodes when the hidraw is opened. However,
this isn't sufficient to avoid FEATURE reports from conflicting, so we
change to fully unregistering the controller internally, leaving only the
hidraw active until it's closed.

This also unifies the unregister and connect callbacks, as now the logic
between these two callbacks is identical.

This also puts work canceling for rumble and mode switch in

patches.name: 0231--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Zero-initialize-reply-in-serial-lookup.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Zero-initialize reply in serial
 lookup
patches.rationale:
When requesting the serial number from a controller, the function will do
some basic bounds checking to make sure the reply is valid, as well as
capping off the reply with a null byte before copying. However, the error
logging can leak uninitialized memory in some cases. We can simplify and
solve this by just zero-initalizing the reply memory eagerly instead.

patches.name: 0232--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Reject-short-reads.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Reject short reads
patches.rationale:
Steam Controller FEATURE reports encode the size of the message in the
message itself. Previously we were trusting that the size reported matched
the size we actually read, leading to a potential issue with short reads.
Instead, we should actually verify the length of the read.

patches.name: 0233--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Retry-send-recv-reports-if-stale.patch

subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Retry send/recv reports if stale
patches.rationale:
Sometimes recv report will reply with a stale result from a previous send
report. Instead of failing out, we should retry them, as they generally

patches.name: 0234--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Refactor-registration.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Refactor registration
patches.rationale:
This refactors and simplifies the registration/unregistration flow. Since
we now only perform registration when the client isn't opened anymore, the
logic for handling that can be removed, and the rest of the function
streamlined.

We also remove the previous assumption that we have a serial number to show
we're registered, replacing it with a single purpose boolean.

In a previous refactor the code for unregistering a battery if later
registration steps failed was accidentally left out. As a result, a
lingering power_supply object could get left over after the steam object
was torn down. This is also fixed here.

patches.name: 0239--FROM-UPSTREAM-HID-steam-Zero-out-inputs-when-disabling-gamepad-mode.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] HID: steam: Zero out inputs when disabling
 gamepad mode
patches.rationale:
When gamepad mode is disabled the gamepad input devices will stop receiving
updates. However, in the case where there are buttons still pressed this
will appear as an indefinitely-held button. Instead we should zero out the
inputs to make it look like things are all released. We do the same thing
for gyroscope inputs to make sure it doesn't look like it's endlessly
rotating, but we freeze the accelerometer input since zero isn't a neutral
input on the surface of the Earth.

patches.name: 0241--FROM-ML-platform-x86-msi-wmi-Add-MSI-Claw-M-Center-keys.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-ML] platform/x86: msi-wmi: Add MSI Claw M-Center keys
patches.rationale:
MSI Claw devices produce WMI events through the MSI WMI hotkeys GUID for
some of their buttons. When pressed, these cause spam in the kernel. For
the majority of devices these events can be safely ignored as they are
duplicated by the AT Translated Set 2 Keyboard device exposed as an
evdev. For the MSI Claw A8 BZ2EM model's M-Center Menu button (left of
the screen) there is no associated keyboard event, so this event must be
exposed. Map this button to the same scancode produced by the AT
Keyboard device on other models. This does cause double F15 events on
the A1M, 7 AI+ A2VM, and 8 AI+ A2VM, but it appears to be harmless in my
testing.

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260613021654.933618-3-derekjohn.clark@gmail.com

patches.name: 0242--FROM-ML-platform-x86-msi-wmi-platform-Use-input-buffer-for-returning-result.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-ML] platform/x86: msi-wmi-platform: Use input buffer
 for returning result
patches.rationale:
Modify msi_wmi_platform_query() to reuse the input buffer for
returning the result of a WMI method call. Using a separate output
buffer to return the result is unnecessary because the WMI interface
requires both buffers to have the same length anyway.

Co-developed-by: Antheas Kapenekakis <lkml@antheas.dev>

patches.name: 0256--FOR-UPSTREAM-ASoC-cs35l41-Restore-register-state-after-system-sleep.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] ASoC: cs35l41: Restore register state after
 system sleep
patches.rationale:
Currently, on the Steam Deck LCD when the system goes into hibernation
and resumes back, the speakers are silent when playing with:

  aplay -D plughw:acp5x,1 /usr/share/sounds/alsa/Front_Left.wav

A crude workaround was to, after resuming the system, bypassing the
regmap cache on the cs35l41 devices, before playing:

  echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/spi-VLV1776\:00/cache_bypass
  echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/spi-VLV1776\:01/cache_bypass

That indicated that the hardware registers had gone out of sync with
the regmap cache due to the power down in system hibernation.

Fix the issue by, before system sleep, marking the regcache as cache
only, and after system sleep, reseting the hardware and restoring the
hardware registers from the regcache.

This gets the sound working on the Steam Deck LCD after resume from S4.

While the issue was only observed on S4 on this platform, the callbacks
for suspend/resume are also set in the same way to account for platforms
that power down the chip on S3 as well.

Note that this change does not take care of restoring the DSP state,
since the affected platform does not use the DSP and it couldn't be
tested, so it is only shut down on resume so it can be reinitialized in
the future.

Assisted-by: GitHub Copilot CLI:claude-sonnet-4.6

patches.name: 0257--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-hid-asus-ally-add-sleep_animation-attr-for-ring-LEDs.patch

patches.name: 0258--FOR-UPSTREAM-cfg80211-add-6-GHz-passive-scan-rule-to-the-world-regulatory-domain.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] cfg80211: add 6 GHz passive-scan rule to the
 world regulatory domain
patches.rationale:
The built-in world domain ("00") has no 6 GHz frequency rules, causing
every 6 GHz channel to be marked IEEE80211_CHAN_DISABLED.  Disabled
channels are silently dropped from scan requests in nl80211, so drivers
never receive them, no beacons are ever heard, and 6 GHz-only networks
are completely invisible regardless of hardware capability.

Add a single NO_IR rule covering the full 6 GHz WiFi band
(UNII-5 through UNII-8, 5945–7125 MHz).  This is consistent with the
treatment of every 5 GHz channel in the world domain, all of which carry
NO_IR rather than being disabled outright.

With NO_IR instead of DISABLED:
  - scan requests include 6 GHz channels in passive (listen-only) mode;
  - when a beacon is received, regulatory_hint_found_beacon() enqueues a
    beacon hint, handle_reg_beacon() clears NO_IR for that channel, and
    NL80211_CMD_REG_BEACON_HINT is delivered to user space;
  - wpa_supplicant / iwd can then associate normally.

This activates the existing beacon-hint path for 6 GHz and requires no
driver changes.  Drivers that already manage their own regulatory domain
(REGULATORY_WIPHY_SELF_MANAGED) are unaffected.

Assisted-by: Claude:Sonnet 4.6

patches.name: 0261--FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amd-display-Always-notify-the-HDA-driver-on-disconnect.patch

patches.name: 0262--FOR-UPSTREAM-ALSA-hda-Force-resume-if-acomp-notified-during-system-suspend.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] ALSA: hda: Force resume if acomp notified
 during system suspend
patches.rationale:
Currently if an HDMI cable is connected while the system is suspended,
the HDMI audio jack status stays off after resume.

This is due to the jack state not being synced by the HDA codec device's
runtime resume, as that never happens if the device was runtime
suspended before the system suspended, or by the acomp notification
triggered from the DRM side if that happens before the HDA codec device
has resumed.

To fix this, if snd_hda_hdmi_acomp_pin_eld_notify() gets called before
the HDA codec device has resumed, queue it to get force resumed (runtime
resumed) at PM complete time.

Do this using a separate acomp_requested_resume flag that can be
temporarily set without overwriting forced_resume for drivers that
always want to force resume.

patches.name: 0263--FOR-UPSTREAM-mmc-rtsx-keep-PCI-function-in-D0-while-an-SD-card-is-present.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] mmc: rtsx: keep PCI function in D0 while an SD
 card is present
patches.rationale:
On handhelds that disable MMC_CAP_AGGRESSIVE_PM via the DMI quirk table,
the mmc core no longer powers the card off on runtime suspend, but the
rtsx function still force-powers-down and delinks it (rts522a:
D3_DELINK_MODE_EN + FPDCTL ALL_POWER_DOWN). The card is reset while the
core still believes it is initialised, so the next request hits dead
silicon: RTS522A reports the card removed ("tuning execution failed: -22"
on retry) and corrupts the filesystem, while RTS525A/RTS5261 get stuck
("Card stuck being busy!", "error -110 doing runtime resume").

Re-enabling aggressive PM is not an option as it reintroduces the resume
re-init stall the quirk was added to avoid. Instead, on those devices,
refuse runtime suspend while an SD card is present:
rtsx_pci_runtime_suspend() returns -EBUSY rather than power-cycling a
card the core still owns, so the function stays in D0.
rtsx_pci_runtime_idle() still runs, so ASPM L1 stays enabled and idle
link power is preserved.

The gate (sd_pm_keepalive) is set by the SD/MMC host and read live at
suspend time, so a card already present at boot is covered regardless of
probe order, and the host clears it on remove so it never outlives the
host. The gate is scoped to the quirked devices, so other systems keep
normal runtime PM; an empty slot still suspends and delinks, and s2idle
still re-inits via the normal ->set_ios() path. An SD-Express handoff
clears the gate so the function can delink for the NVMe device.

Fixes: 9a626290791b ("[FOR-UPSTREAM] mmc: rtsx: add quirk table to disable runtime power management")
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4-8

patches.name: 0266--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-ACPI-battery-derive-present-rate-from-capacity-change-on-MSI-Claw-8-EX-AI-.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] ACPI: battery: derive present rate from
 capacity change on MSI Claw 8 EX AI+
patches.rationale:
The EC on the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ (board MS-1T91, BIOS E1T91IMS.105) reports
a bogus _BST present rate that does not track load. Measured live, current_now
held at ~-63 A across a 60s window in which charge_now actually moved from
2037 mAh to 1996 mAh, a real discharge of 2.46 A (~37.6 W). The EC value is
off by ~25x here and by a different factor under other loads, so no constant
scale corrects it; the reported rate simply never moves.

Everything that reads current_now/power_now (MangoHUD, the Steam UI) then
reports a nonsensical draw. Add a DMI-gated quirk that derives the rate from
the change in remaining capacity over time, recomputed when the capacity
counter ticks and held steady in between. Report 0 while the pack is neither
charging nor discharging, so it does not show a stale draw when full and
plugged in.

Holo: Drop this quirk when MSI fixes the EC firmware.

patches.name: 0268--FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-Mask-Replay-Timer-Timeout-errors-for-Realtek-RTS5264.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI: Mask Replay Timer Timeout errors for
 Realtek RTS5264
patches.rationale:
Like the Genesys GL975x, the Realtek RTS5264 SD card reader floods
Replay Timer Timeout correctable errors under ASPM. Mask them the same
way the GL975x quirk already does.

Two things differ from the GL975x and shape the fixup. The RTS5264
reports the errors itself, through its own Transmitter ID rather than
its upstream Port, so mask them on the device. And the reader shares its
Port with SD Express cards through a mux and is hot-added whenever such a
card is removed, so the errors can begin as soon as pci_aer_init()
enables reporting, ahead of any final fixup. Mask in a header fixup,
which precedes pci_aer_init() in both the boot and hot-add paths; the AER
capability offset is not cached that early, so look it up when needed.

ASPM stays enabled.

patches.name: 0269--FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-ASPM-Reconfigure-bridge-LTR-when-a-device-arrives-with-LTR-enabled.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI/ASPM: Reconfigure bridge LTR when a device
 arrives with LTR enabled
patches.rationale:
pci_configure_ltr() assumes a device found with LTR already enabled was
set up by firmware together with the rest of the path, and only caches
ltr_path for it. But a hot-added device can also arrive with LTR
enabled, because its configuration may survive removal: an SD Express
card reader muxes either itself or the card's NVMe controller onto the
link, and hands the link back to the reader with its earlier
configuration, including the LTR enable, intact.

Hot removal disables LTR in the bridge, so every LTR message such a
device sends is handled as an Unsupported Request (PCIe r6.0, sec 6.18):

  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Uncorrectable (Non-Fatal), type=Transaction Layer, (Requester ID)
  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: device [8086:e43a] error status/mask=00100000/00004000
  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: [20] UnsupReq (First)
  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: TLP Header: 0x34000000 0x56000010 0x00009003 0x00000000
  rtsx_pci 0000:56:00.0: AER: can't recover (no error_detected callback)

The TLP header decodes as an LTR message from the device. Reconfigure
LTR in the bridge, as the hot-add path already does.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

patches.name: 0270--FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-PM-Keep-MSI-Claw-8-EX-AI-SD-Express-slot-Port-out-of-runtime-D3.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI/PM: Keep MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ SD Express slot
 Port out of runtime D3
patches.rationale:
The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ routes its microSD Express slot to Root Port
0000:00:1c.0 through a Realtek RTS5264 card reader. The reader muxes
either itself (UHS-I cards) or the card's own NVMe controller (SD
Express cards) onto the link, so slot presence is in-band only: the
Port learns of a card solely from the link coming up.

The platform provides RTD3 methods for the Port, so bridge D3 is
otherwise allowed, but neither D3hot nor D3cold keeps link detection
alive, and no wake event is generated when a card is inserted or when
the reader takes the link back after an SD Express card is removed.
Once the Port runtime suspends with the link down, the slot is dead
until a manual rescan or reboot:

  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: pciehp: Slot(2): Link Down
  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: pciehp: Slot(2): Card present
  pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: pciehp: Slot(2): No link

Add no_runtime_d3 to struct pci_dev, making the port service driver
refuse runtime suspend when set, and set it for this Port on this
machine. With the Port awake, switching between UHS-I and SD Express
cards works reliably in both directions.

Only runtime D3 is blocked: making pci_bridge_d3_possible() return
false would also keep the Port in D0 across system sleep, because
pci_power_manageable() gates the suspend path on bridge_d3, and that
hangs s2idle entry on this platform. System sleep needs no such
restriction; pciehp re-checks presence on resume.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

patches.name: 0271--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-Reset-Realtek-RTS5264-link-when-it-comes-back-degraded.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI: Reset Realtek RTS5264 link when it
 comes back degraded
patches.rationale:
The RTS5264 shares its Port with SD Express cards through a mux: the
card's own NVMe controller owns the link while such a card is inserted,
and the link is handed back to the reader when the card is removed.

The handed-back link regularly comes up degraded: stuck at 2.5GT/s
below the supported speed, streaming corrected errors from both ends at
thousands per second in bursts. Retraining does not recover it and the
link refuses higher speeds; only a Secondary Bus Reset, taking the
LTSSM back through Detect, restores an error-free link at full speed.

The degradation often develops only after the reader has enumerated
cleanly, so a single check at enumeration time misses it. Check the
link a few seconds after every runtime hot-add of the reader instead,
from a workqueue, using the evidence accumulated by then: a link stuck
below the supported speed, receiver-side corrected errors on the
reader, or replay churn on the Port. If any is present, remove the
reader, reset the secondary bus, and rescan under the rescan/remove
lock. Wait for the link after the reset: the bus is childless at that
point, so the reset helper cannot, and the rescan would race link
training. The subsequent hot-add schedules another check, verifying
the recovery; resets are rate-limited in case the link stays degraded
regardless.

Only runtime hand-backs are reset. A link that is already degraded
when firmware trained it at boot (for instance by the electrical load
of an SD Express card left sitting in the slot in UHS mode) is not
recoverable this way.

Holo: this one should probably be fixed by Realtek, but for now we need
this for SD express support on MSI Claw 8 EX AI+.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

patches.name: 0272--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-ASPM-force-L1-support-on-MSI-Claw-8-EX-AI-RTS5264-root-port.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI/ASPM: force L1 support on MSI Claw 8
 EX AI+ RTS5264 root port
patches.rationale:
The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ BIOS E1T91IMS.105 advertises only ASPM L0s in the
Link Capabilities of the PCH PCIe root port (8086:e43a) that hosts the
RTS5264 SD card reader, even though the port supports ASPM L1 and L1 PM
substates. Because the ASPM core therefore leaves aspm_l1_support clear,
it never programs L1/L1SS on the link, the port's PMC power-gate domain
never gates, and the SoC can never reach S0ix during s2idle.

The port's read-only capability registers are self-inconsistent. Its
Link Capabilities register (CAP_EXP+0x0c) reads 0x03736413, ASPM
Support = L0s only, while its L1 PM Substates capability (0x204) reads
0x00293c3f, advertising ASPM L1.1 and L1.2 as supported. The downstream
RTS5264 advertises ASPM L1 in its own Link Capabilities, so only the
root port under-reports.

Add a DMI-gated header fixup that marks the root port L1-capable so the
ASPM core programs the L1.2 timing on the link.

Holo: this one should likely be fixed in the BIOS by MSI/Intel.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

patches.name: 0273--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-mmc-rtsx-enable-ASPM-L1.2-on-MSI-Claw-8-EX-AI-to-reach-S0ix.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] mmc: rtsx: enable ASPM L1.2 on MSI Claw 8
 EX AI+ to reach S0ix
patches.rationale:
On the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, BIOS E1T91IMS.105 leaves ASPM L1/L1 substates
disabled on the RTS5264 card-reader's PCIe root port, and the FADT
withholds OS ASPM control (IAPC_BOOT_ARCH = 0x0012, bit 4 set), so the
PCIe core never enables L1.2 on the link. Without L1.2 the driver forces
CLKREQ# low and the root-port PMC power-gate domain never gates,
blocking SoC S0ix in s2idle.

On this board, release CLKREQ# (force_clkreq_0 = false) and enable ASPM L1
plus L1 substates on both ends of the link directly, so it can enter L1.2
without the global pcie_aspm=force boot parameter. The L1.2 timing is
already programmed by the PCIe core; a companion PCI quirk marks the root
port L1-capable.

Holo: this one should likely be fixed by MSI/Intel in firmware, like the
preceding commit.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

patches.name: 0274--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-ASPM-enable-L1.2-on-MSI-Claw-8-EX-AI-SD-Express-card-link.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI/ASPM: enable L1.2 on MSI Claw 8 EX AI+
 SD Express card link
patches.rationale:
When an SD Express card is inserted, the RTS5264 hands its link to the
card's own NVMe controller and drops off the bus, so the rtsx driver
quirk that enables ASPM L1.2 on this board never runs: the card's link
stays in L0, the Root Port's PMC power-gate domain never gates, and the
SoC cannot reach S0ix while a card is inserted. The underlying firmware
cause is the same as the companion quirks: the FADT withholds OS ASPM
control (IAPC_BOOT_ARCH = 0x0012, bit 4 set), so the PCIe core will not
enable L1.2 itself.

Enable L1 and the L1 substates on both ends of the link when an NVMe
controller is enumerated below the card reader's Root Port, mirroring
what the rtsx driver does for the reader itself.

Holo: this one should likely be fixed in the BIOS by MSI/Intel.

patches.name: 0275--FOR-UPSTREAM-PCI-PM-Remove-the-device-from-the-PME-poll-list-in-pci_destroy_dev-.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] PCI/PM: Remove the device from the PME poll
 list in pci_destroy_dev()
patches.rationale:
pci_stop_dev() removes the device from the PME poll list before
releasing its driver, but the device can end up back on it: a runtime
suspend racing with the driver release re-enables PME polling through
pci_finish_runtime_suspend(), and for a surprise-removed device the
balancing disable on the resume side never runs. The stale list entry
then outlives the device, and the next pci_pme_list_scan() dereferences
freed memory:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: 0000000b00000040
  Workqueue: events_freezable pci_pme_list_scan
  RIP: 0010:pci_pme_list_scan+0x40/0x210

Observed on the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+: its SD Express slot hot-removes the
RTS5264 card reader, a PME polling device, whenever a card muxes the
reader off the bus, and the reader is usually runtime suspended at that
point.

Remove the device from the poll list again in pci_destroy_dev() after
device_del() has permanently shut runtime PM down, so nothing can
re-enable polling afterwards.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

patches.name: 0276--FOR-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-regd-stop-gating-6GHz-on-the-ww-domain.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: regd: stop gating 6GHz on the ww
 domain
patches.rationale:
The driver maintains its own block_* bitmaps on top of cfg80211's
regulatory enforcement. These bitmaps are indexed by the position of an
entry in the active regd_map (either the built-in rtw89_regd_map or the
table loaded from a firmware element).

The ww domain is handled outside the regd_map; it lives in a standalone
rtw89_ww_regd object, and rtw89_regd_get_index() returns the
RTW89_REGD_MAX_COUNTRY_NUM sentinel for it. Every block_* lookup site
guards against that sentinel and bails out, which means none of the
block_* checks ever apply to ww. The 6GHz check therefore treats ww as
unconditionally blocked at the driver layer, independently of whatever
cfg80211/wireless-regdb permit.

Make ww a first-class entry in the regd_map instead:

- Reserve slot 0 of rtw89_regd_map for the ww entry and drop the
  standalone rtw89_ww_regd object.
- In rtw89_recognize_regd_from_elm(), reserve slot 0 of the
  firmware-loaded map for ww and populate it from the built-in
  definition via the new rtw89_regd_static_ww_entry() helper.
- Drop the rtw89_regd_is_ww() special case in rtw89_regd_get_index()
  and identify ww by alpha2 so the check works for entries in either
  map.
- Have rtw89_regd_find_reg_by_name() return NULL on miss instead of
  silently substituting ww. Callers that need the previous "fall back
  to ww" behaviour (rtw89_regd_notifier_apply()) now do so explicitly
  against the active map's slot 0, and rtw89_regd_get_index_by_name()
  translates NULL into the RTW89_REGD_MAX_COUNTRY_NUM sentinel so the
  existing "unknown alpha2" branches in the block_* setup paths
  remain.

With ww at a real index the driver's block_* checks apply uniformly for
all bands and cfg80211 / wireless-regdb become the sole source of truth
for what is permitted on the ww domain.

patches.name: 0292--FROM-ML-drm-amd-display-Restore-ALLM-support-in-HDMI-vsif.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-ML] drm/amd/display: Restore ALLM support in HDMI vsif
patches.rationale:
[Why]
Support for triggering ALLM in modern TVs is missing.

When HDMI vsif was added in 2019:
commit 3c2381b92cba ("drm/amd/display: add support for VSIP info packet")
it was improperly handeled as HDMI actually has two separate vsifs. The
implementation was based on H14b-vsif and ALLM bit was messing it up
because H14b-vsif doesn't support ALLM. It was later removed in:
commit 75f77aafe281 ("drm/amd/display: Send H14b-VSIF specified in HDMI")

ALLM is supported by hf-vsif (HDMI Forum) instead.

[How]
Add proper logic to construct either h14b-vsif or hf-vsif based on
required capabilities. Currently, only ALLM from hf-vsif is supported.

Turns out, hf-vsif is almost identical to h14b-vsif, BUT has additional
two bytes of data after OUI. First byte is static and seems like
a version supported by leftover define. Second byte consists of 3D and
ALLM bits.

Implement logic to offset 3D data if building hf-vsif.

[How]

be indicated in HDMI Forum vsif. Additionally, make sure VIC modes are
translated in case of ALLM active as VIC cannot be used in conjunction
with hf-vsif. I learned this the hard way...

subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-ML] drm/amd/display: freesync_on_desktop support for
 HDMI VRR
patches.rationale:
[Why]
Many TVs and other HDMI sinks suffer from blanking and possibly other
glitches when VRR is toggled. With FreeSync present on such sinks, they
behave like the signal is always variable, even in fixed refresh rate
situations. DisplayPort and eDP enforce seamless VRR transitions but
HDMI unfortunately doesn't.

[How]

Add logic that control this behavior and use this mode by default until
it can be controlled by connector KMS property.

Functionally, for an end user, this is the same as normal, fixed refresh
rate mode. The only difference is that sink is kept in VRR state which
enables seamless transitions into/out of variable refresh rate.

Uses the already established freesync_on_desktop field and logic.

patches.name: 0305--FROM-ML-wifi-ath11k-cap-out-of-range-rx-MCS-instead-of-leaving-bogus-rate.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-ML] wifi: ath11k: cap out-of-range rx MCS instead of
 leaving bogus rate
patches.rationale:
ath11k can receive HT/VHT/HE frames whose reported MCS is above the
maximum that can be expressed in the corresponding mac80211 rate space
(e.g. an HE frame reported with MCS 12, while HE tops out at MCS 11).

The frame itself is valid and decodes correctly, but for such a frame
ath11k_dp_rx_h_rate() leaves rx_status->rate_idx set to the out-of-range
value and never assigns rx_status->encoding, so it stays RX_ENC_LEGACY
from the ath11k_dp_rx_h_ppdu() initialization. Once that frame reaches
mac80211 it trips the rate sanity check and the frame is dropped with a
splat:

  ath11k_pci 0000:03:00.0: Received with invalid mcs in HE mode 12
  WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 0 at net/mac80211/rx.c:5433 ieee80211_rx_list+0xb0a/0xe90 [mac80211]

Dropping the frame would discard otherwise valid data, so instead cap the
reported MCS to the maximum the rate space can express and deliver the
frame. Set rx_status->encoding before the range check and assign rate_idx
from the capped value, so a frame with an out-of-range MCS no longer
leaves partial or bogus rate metadata behind. Also downgrade the logging
level since they are not treated as invalid frames now. The only loss is
that such a frame is reported as the capped MCS in the rx rate statistics.

Tested-on: WCN6855 hw2.1 PCI WLAN.HSP.1.1-03125-QCAHSPSWPL_V1_V2_SILICONZ_LITE-3.6510.41

Fixes: d5c65159f289 ("ath11k: driver for Qualcomm IEEE 802.11ax devices")

patches.name: 0312--FROM-ML-PCI-Add-quirk-for-ID-mutation-of-MSI-Claw-A8-cardreader.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-ML] PCI: Add quirk for ID mutation of MSI Claw A8
 cardreader
patches.rationale:
Derek reports a lockup on resume of the MSI Claw A8 if a card is inserted
into the onboard Realtek RTS525A cardreader.  He has root-caused it to a
mutation of the cardreader's Subsystem Vendor and Device ID:  Firmware
sets an MSI-specific ID on boot, but neglects to reset it on resume.
The ID thus changes to the generic Realtek Vendor and Device ID.

The firmware also incorrectly sets the Hot-Plug Capable bit on the Root
Port and the PCIe hotplug driver interprets the ID mutation as removal of
the cardreader during system sleep (see pciehp_device_replaced()).

The lockup is caused by the block layer being unaware of the hot-removal
and waiting indefinitely in sync_filesystem().  That is fixed with a
separate commit for the cardreader driver.  However despite that other
commit, the cardreader is still hot-removed and re-enumerated the first
time the system is put to sleep.  This is undesirable because it prevents
using an MMC card as root filesystem.

Avoid hot-removal of the cardreader by mutating the cached copy of the
Subsystem Vendor and Device ID.  This needs to be done before going to
sleep, not afterwards, because pci_pm_resume_noirq() is executed top-down
across the hierarchy and hence a pci_fixup_resume_early quirk of the
cardreader would run after hot-removal at its parent Root Port.

In the unlikely event that a fixed firmware becomes available, the quirk
can either be reverted or constrained to specific BIOS versions by way of
a dmi_get_date() conditional.

Reported-by: Derek J. Clark <derekjohn.clark@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Derek J. Clark <derekjohn.clark@gmail.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260806214808.1202819-1-derekjohn.clark@gmail.com/
Link: https://github.com/ValveSoftware/SteamOS/issues/2473

patches.name: 0313--FROM-ML-mmc-rtsx_pci-Cope-with-hot-removal-of-MMC-host.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-ML] mmc: rtsx_pci: Cope with hot-removal of MMC host
patches.rationale:
Derek reports a lockup on hot-removal of a PCI-attached Realtek RTS525A
MMC host if a card is inserted.  He has root-caused it to the block
layer being unaware of the hot-removal and waiting indefinitely in
sync_filesystem().

For comparison, the NVMe subsystem copes with hot-removal by setting the
controller state to NVME_CTRL_DEAD in nvme_remove(), which in turn leads
to blk_mark_disk_dead() being called from nvme_mark_namespaces_dead().
That avoids the indefinite wait in sync_filesystem().

Adopt this approach:  Detect hot-removal in rtsx_pci_sdmmc_drv_remove()
and invoke a new mmc_host_set_removed() helper which in turn invokes
mmc_card_set_removed().  Before flushing outstanding requests to the
card in mmc_blk_remove_req(), check for its removal and call
blk_mark_disk_dead().

Note that mmc_card_set_removed() cannot be called from the MMC host
driver because it is private to the MMC core, hence the indirection
through the newly introduced mmc_host_set_removed() helper.

Other removable MMC hosts, in particular if attached via PCI or USB,
may need to be amended with a similar check for hot-removal.  The
present commit seeks to get that process going.

Reported-by: Derek J. Clark <derekjohn.clark@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Derek J. Clark <derekjohn.clark@gmail.com>

patches.name: 0332--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-drop-packet-offload-entry-on-H2C-addition-failure-to-avoid-scan-issue.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: drop packet offload entry on H2C
 addition failure to avoid scan issue
patches.rationale:
A special case is when C2H done ack has been completed, but the
corresponding packet offload response has not actually been received,
which causes the add packet offload to fail. In this state, firmware
treats the entry as added, so subsequent add requests for the same id
are rejected as duplicates. To recover from this, send a delete packet
offload H2C command to roll back the normal state. It has been tested and
verified to have no functional side effect.

patches.name: 0333--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-disable-sniffer-mode-in-RX-filter-when-initialization-for-Wi-Fi-7-chi.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: disable sniffer mode in RX
 filter when initialization for Wi-Fi 7 chips
patches.rationale:
Sniffer mode is enabled by default in the RX filter on Wi-Fi 7 chips,
which causes all packets to be received regardless of the ADDR_CAM
lookup result. This may result in unexpected packets being received.
Therefore, disable it by default.

patches.name: 0334--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-pci-disable-phy-error-flag-related-to-refclk.patch

subjects:

patches.name: 0335--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-fw-fix-link-ID-filling-for-LPS-MLO-common-info.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history

patches.name: 0336--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-wow-use-MLD-address-in-WoWLAN-ARP-replies-for-MLO-stations.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: wow: use MLD address in WoWLAN
 ARP replies for MLO stations
patches.rationale:
Currently, WoWLAN ARP replies for MLO stations use the link address in
the ARP hardware address fields.

As a result, peers may learn the link address from the ARP reply and
use it as the destination address for subsequent traffic. Some APs may
not forward frames addressed to the link address, causing connectivity
issues.

Use the MLD address instead when generating WoWLAN ARP replies so peers
learn the correct address for MLO stations.

patches.name: 0337--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-wow-add-QoS-control-field-to-WoWLAN-ARP-response-for-MLO.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: wow: add QoS control field to
 WoWLAN ARP response for MLO
patches.rationale:
Some MLO APs expect WoWLAN ARP response frames to be transmitted as
QoS data frames and may discard frames that do not contain a QoS
Control field.

Add a QoS Control field and use the QoS Data subtype when generating
WoWLAN ARP responses for MLD vifs. Keep the existing frame format
unchanged for non-MLO connections.

This allows WoWLAN ARP responses to be accepted by MLO APs while
preserving compatibility with legacy APs.

patches.name: 0338--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-wow-only-WiFi-6-chips-initialize-RF-registers-in-WoWLAN-mode.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: wow: only WiFi 6 chips
 initialize RF registers in WoWLAN mode
patches.rationale:
Only the WiFi 6 chips need to initialize RF register when WoWLAN download
FW for some power save issue. Applying the same initialization flow to
WiFi 7 chips might trigger the error
'RF parameters exceed size. path=1, idx=1500.'.

This happens because normal mode uses rtw89_phy_config_rf_reg_v1(), which
skips registers with addresses below 0x100. However, WoWLAN mode uses
rtw89_phy_config_rf_reg_noio(), and WiFi 7 chips do not satisfy the
rtw89_chip_rf_v1() condition. As a result, more RF registers are
configured, causing the size overflow error.

patches.name: 0339--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-check-return-values-in-rtw89_ops_start_ap-.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history

subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: check return values in

patches.rationale:
Several functions called in rtw89_ops_start_ap() may fail to allocate
skb or fail to send H2C command to firmware, returning -ENOMEM or an

Fixes: a52e4f2ce0f5 ("rtw89: implement ieee80211_ops::start_ap and stop_ap")

patches.name: 0351--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-8922d-dynamic-adjust-channel-smoothing.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history

[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: 8922d: dynamic adjust channel

Add support for path difference based channel smoothing for RTL8922D chip.
This feature measures the ratio of NDP frames and uses a moving average

patches.name: 0352--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-8922d-fix-EMLSR-BB-switch-sequence-for-MLO-mode-transition.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: 8922d: fix EMLSR BB switch
 sequence for MLO mode transition
patches.rationale:
Assert BB reset in the intermediate "switch to 1+1" step of the EMLSR
switch sequence for all three MLO mode transitions by updating the
B_EMLSR_SWITCH_BE4 intermediate value from 0xAFFF to 0x3BAB.

Without the BB reset in this step, the baseband can be left in an
inconsistent state before settling into the final MLO configuration.

patches.name: 0353--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-phy-fix-bandedge-primary-channel-for-2.4GHz-40MHz-and-6GHz.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: phy: fix bandedge primary
 channel for 2.4GHz 40MHz and 6GHz

patches.name: 0354--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-8922d-set-TX-compensation-by-format-v2.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: 8922d: set TX compensation by
 format v2
patches.rationale:
The total number of TX compensation registers is 22, including 7 base and
15 ones according to operating channel.

The v0 is 22 ones per channel. To reduce array size, v1 treats 7 base as
common part across all conditions. However, we can fine tune the base part
to yield better performance, so divide base into two sets according to NSS.
Summarize dimensions as follows

	base (7)		vals(15)
  v0	nss * band * path	nss * band * path
  v1	1			nss * band * path
  v2	nss			nss * band * path

Currently, v1 and v2 can present in a file, but only one fw element with
a specific format will be used for specific RFE type.

patches.name: 0357--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-8922d-read-default-digital-voltage-calibration-values.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: 8922d: read default digital
 voltage calibration values
patches.rationale:
In order to lower temperature when WiFi is running, reduce the digital
voltage for the purpose.

The calibration values of digital voltage are programmed in efuse. One is
for normal use, which driver stores it into hal->thermal_prot_vmax. The
other is the minimum voltage, which is stored into hal->thermal_prot_vmin.
These two values define a range of supported voltage, which latter patch
uses them to adjust voltage depends on thermal value (temperature).

patches.name: 0358--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-add-thermal-protect-by-digital-voltage-reduction.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: add thermal protect by digital
 voltage reduction
patches.rationale:
The temperature is rising when WiFi does high throughput, and reduce
voltage is a way to ease temperature.

The existing method to do thermal protect is to reduce TX duty, which
can affect throughput obviously. Before doing reduce TX duty (with -20
thermal value offset), driver does voltage reduction first, which doesn't
affect throughput but lower power consumption.

The voltage gram of register is 0.01 voltage, and the suggested maximum
reduction is 6 grams, which driver defines 6 as maximum voltage level.
When thermal value is over threshold, driver will try to adjust level and
corresponding register value. It should be adjust grams one by one with
additional 50 ms delay to ensure hardware work properly.

A note that the voltage must reset to normal value before entering power
save mode, otherwise WiFi card might get lost. Since it takes 50 ms delay
for each gram to adjust voltage, we stop to enter power save if protect
level is not zero.

By the way, adjust thermal threshold to 0xB4 as desired.

patches.name: 0378--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-8922d-add-TX-time-limit-for-2GHz-band.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: 8922d: add TX time limit for
 2GHz band
patches.rationale:
Fix 2.4GHz specific L-SIG length TX issue, causing interoperability problem
with certain APs. Limit the A-MPDU duration to be workaround.

For 8922DE, the MAC limit is 164 ticks, and BB limit is 4608 us. The
conversion is 32.768us / tick. Since smaller limit should be adopted,
BB limit is filled into newly added field.

The units of register and CCTL table are tick and us/512 respectively.
Convert to target unit when filling values.

patches.name: 0380--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-add-tx-shape-v0-to-keep-built-in-arrays-compatible-during-transitions.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: add tx shape v0 to keep built-in
 arrays compatible during transitions
patches.rationale:
TX shape parameters can come from (old way) built-in arrays or (new way)
FW elements. The built-in arrays will no longer be updated, but will be
retained during a certain transition period. However, the format of newer
TX shape parameters are going to be expanded. It will only be applied to
FW elements. To keep built-in arrays compatible during transition period,
add tx shape v0 for old format.

The v0 fields can be removed along with built-in arrays once transition
period ends.

patches.name: 0381--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-extend-tx-shape-format-for-regulatory-6-GHz-power-type.patch

subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: extend tx shape format for
 regulatory 6 GHz power type
patches.rationale:
Even under the same regulation, TX shape may need different settings for
different 6 GHz power types. So, add one more dimension for that. Because
TX shape parameters are not quite large, the 2/5/6 GHz sections are not
divided into different structures. So, the 2/5 GHz sections will also get
the new dimension. To 2/5 GHz sections, fill the TX shape settings with
RTW89_REG_6GHZ_POWER_DFLT (0) field.

patches.name: 0385--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-fw-use-MAC-source-for-IO-offload-delay-command.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: fw: use MAC source for IO
 offload delay command
patches.rationale:
The udelay/mdelay helpers set the command source to
RTW89_FW_CMD_OFLD_SRC_OTHER (4), which does not fit the two-bit field
RTW89_H2C_CMD_OFLD_W0_SRC (GENMASK(1, 0)). The le32_encode_bits() masks
it down to 0 (RTW89_FW_CMD_OFLD_SRC_BB), and compiler throws
__field_overflow() error. Fortunately it still works because firmware
ignores the source field for a delay command.

Use RTW89_FW_CMD_OFLD_SRC_MAC as the vendor driver does, and drop the
unused RTW89_FW_CMD_OFLD_SRC_OTHER enumerator.

Reported-by: Bitterblue Smith <rtl8821cerfe2@gmail.com>
Closes: https://github.com/morrownr/rtw89/issues/111
Fixes: ae3d327515f2 ("wifi: rtw89: add IO offload support via firmware")

patches.name: 0386--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-add-LED-support-to-reflect-the-wireless-association-status.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: add LED support to reflect the
 wireless association status
patches.rationale:
Add a new RTW89_LEDS Kconfig option, along with LED structures to describe
flexible GPIO mappings for chip common LED definition. Core LED lifecycle
and registration logic default to the mac80211 association trigger, and
chips are wired up as the first user with a single-GPIO monochrome LED.

Usage:
- Auto-triggered (default):
  ON when connected, OFF when disconnected
- Manual override:
    echo <1|0> > /sys/class/leds/rtw89-phyX/brightness

patches.name: 0387--FROM-UPSTREAM-wifi-rtw89-add-multicolor-LED-support-for-RTL8852CU-valve-board.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-UPSTREAM] wifi: rtw89: add multicolor LED support for
 RTL8852CU valve board
patches.rationale:
Add multicolor LED support for the RTL8852CU valve board to reflect
wireless connection status (by default, green LED is ON when associated
and OFF when disconnected).

Extend the rtw89 LED subsystem with a multicolor path via led_classdev_mc,
for board-level variants with more than one LED GPIO channel.

Add a new RTW89_LEDS_MC Kconfig option and support multicolor LEDs
through led_classdev_mc, with per-channel caching to minimize
redundant register writes. The RTL8852CU valve board is wired up as
the first user, driving a multicolor WRGB LED over four GPIO channels
(8, 18, 16, and 17) that map to LED_COLOR_ID_WHITE/RED/GREEN/BLUE.

Usage:
- Auto-triggered (default):
  Green LED ON when connected, OFF when disconnected

- Manual override (e.g., set red; channel order: WHITE RED GREEN BLUE):
    echo "0 1 0 0" > /sys/class/leds/rtw89-phyX-multicolor/multi_intensity
    echo 1         > /sys/class/leds/rtw89-phyX-multicolor/brightness

patches.name: 0415--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amd-display-debugfs-UCLK-floor-via-the-DAL-hard-min.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/amd/display: debugfs UCLK floor via
 the DAL hard-min
patches.rationale:
HDMI audio on Navi 33 (DCN 3.2.1) drops out in a frame-locked pattern
whenever the memory clock changes DPM level.  Holding UCLK at any single
frequency eliminates the dropouts entirely, including the lowest DPM
state, so the level itself is harmless and only the switch blackout
matters.  Restricting DPM to the top two levels works as well, which fits
a blackout whose length scales with the size of the clock step.

The obvious userspace workarounds all have side effects.  Masking levels
through pp_dpm_mclk requires AMD_DPM_FORCED_LEVEL_MANUAL, and
smu_switch_power_profile() drops every request while that level is set,
so the GFX ring can no longer bump the workload profile and VR, VIDEO and
COMPUTE profiles stop being selected.  The OverDrive UclkFmin knob avoids
manual mode but is not exposed on every board, and enabling OverDrive at
all makes amdgpu_gfx_profile_ring_begin_use() return early, losing profile
switching just as thoroughly.  Clearing the DPM_UCLK feature bit works but
parks the clock at its minimum with no way to choose a floor.

DC already asks the SMU for a UCLK hard-min over the DAL mailbox, which is
independent of the powerplay forced performance level.  Add
dc->debug.min_uclk_mhz and clamp every UCLK hard-min in the DCN 3.2 clock
manager to it, giving a memory clock floor that leaves workload profile
switching untouched.

Clamping alone is not enough to make the floor usable.
dcn32_update_clocks() only re-sends a hard-min when the requested dram
clock changes, so a display sitting at a steady frequency never picks up
a newly written floor.  Add dc_set_min_uclk_mhz(), which stores the floor
and pushes it out immediately through the existing set_min_memclk clock
manager op.

Also record the value actually sent as dc->uclk_hard_min_mhz_requested
and expose it read-only, so a floor that has not been applied is
distinguishable from one the SMU declined.

Two debugfs files, amdgpu_dm_min_uclk_mhz and
amdgpu_dm_uclk_hard_min_requested_mhz.  Whether the SMU honours a DAL
hard-min is visible in pp_dpm_mclk.

DCN 3.2 and 3.2.1 share dcn32_clk_mgr.c, so both are covered; dcn401 is
not.

patches.name: 0416--FROM-ML-drm-amdgpu-Disable-runtime-PM-for-externally-attached-dGPUs.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FROM-ML] drm/amdgpu: Disable runtime PM for externally
 attached dGPUs
patches.rationale:
pci_is_thunderbolt_attached() requires an upstream PCI bridge with
is_thunderbolt set from an Intel Thunderbolt VSEC. This does not cover
the affected ASM4242 USB4 PCI hierarchy:

  00:02.2
    \- 0f:00.0 [1b21:2421]
       +- 10:01.0 [1b21:2423] -> 45:00.0 -> 46:00.0
       |  -> 47:00.0 -> 48:00.0 -> 49:00.0 [1002:7590]
       \- 10:03.0 -> 76:00.0 [1b21:2425] USB4 Host Router

The host router is outside the GPU upstream bridge chain, leaving no
ancestor with is_thunderbolt set. PCI core propagates DEVICE_REMOVABLE
below the external-facing PCIe tunnel. Disable Runtime PM when either
pci_is_thunderbolt_attached() or dev_is_removable() is true.

patches.name: 0417--FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amd-display-kick-a-VRR-OTG-out-of-the-extended-vblank-after-a-GPU-reset.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/amd/display: kick a VRR OTG out of the
 extended vblank after a GPU reset
patches.rationale:
With VRR active, the OTG is left parked deep in the DRR-extended vblank
(near v_total_max) after the in-reset restore. On DCN the v_total_min
apply that ends an extended frame is masked to a TRIGA (surface-update)
event. The in-reset restore re-arms DRR with v_total still extended and
its full-surface update re-triggers with that same extended v_total, so
the OTG keeps scanning the extended frame. It never wraps past the
vupdate point and never raises VUPDATE_NO_LOCK, which the vupdate_no_lock
rework made the sole DCN vblank and flip completion source. The flip
submitted across the reset never completes (flip_done timeout) and the
display wedges until a modeset reprograms the timing.

Add dc_force_drr_frame() to collapse v_total to base with
set_vtotal_min_max() and pulse the manual trigger, so the OTG applies the
base v_total, completes a frame, and resumes raising VUPDATE_NO_LOCK.
Call it for active VRR OTGs at the end of dm_resume()'s in-reset path.

patches.name: 0418--FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amd-display-keep-VUPDATE_NO_LOCK-armed-across-a-GPU-reset-on-all-DCN.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/amd/display: keep VUPDATE_NO_LOCK armed
 across a GPU reset on all DCN
patches.rationale:
The vupdate_no_lock rework made VUPDATE_NO_LOCK the sole source of
vblank and pageflip completion on DCN, but manage_dm_interrupts() only
holds an amdgpu vupdate IRQ reference for DCN 3.0.x and 3.2.0. On the
other DCN versions, such as 3.5, the reference is not held, so after a
GPU reset amdgpu_irq_gpu_reset_resume_helper() re-applies the source
from a refcount of zero and leaves it disabled. The pipe then has no
completion source at all (OTG_GLOBAL_SYNC_STATUS.VUPDATE_NO_LOCK_INT_EN
reads 0 post-reset), which shows up as a permanent flip_done timeout on
the next page flip after recovery.

Hold the vupdate reference on all DCN so the source survives the reset.
The DCN 3.0.x and 3.2.0 switch is now only needed to gate the vline0
reference used by secure display.

patches.name: 0419--FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amd-display-Wait-for-flip-completion-before-cleaning-up-fbs.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.

[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/amd/display: Wait for flip completion
 before cleaning up fbs
patches.rationale:
When performing async flips, we can dispatch the flip without waiting
for vblank, but we still need to actually wait for the flip. Otherwise
the framebuffer objects are unpinned too early and things to way south
if we happen to be under memory pressure and try evicting the
framebuffers.

patches.name: 0420--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amdgpu-Track-suboptimal-always-valid-BOs-in-soft-evicted-state.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/amdgpu: Track suboptimal always-valid
 BOs in soft-evicted state
patches.rationale:
The VM state machine would currently not bother checking if VRAM|GTT BOs
marked with VM_ALWAYS_VALID were actually in VRAM (their preferred
placement). This caused those buffers to never be moved back to VRAM if
they were ever spilled to GTT.

Simply moving them to the existing evicted state incurs too much
overhead. Instead, introduce a new "soft-evicted" state for user BOs
that are in a technically suboptimal domain but are still allowed to
reside in that domain. On each submission, an attempt is made to move
these buffers back to the optimal domain, but we bail out immediately if
that ever fails, so as to not unnecessarily try moving things around.

patches.name: 0421--FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-exec-Add-helper-to-bypass-IGNORE_DUPLICATES-flag.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/exec: Add helper to bypass
 IGNORE_DUPLICATES flag
patches.rationale:
TTM is about to switch to drm_exec for locking objects
in the LRU list. When we're done processing the object, we want to
unlock it only if the caller doesn't already hold that lock. If
DRM_EXEC_IGNORE_DUPLICATES is set on the exec object (which callers may
require for unrelated reasons), we have no way of knowing whether the
lock is already held.

To remedy this, add a separate helper that forcefully bypasses the
IGNORE_DUPLICATES flag for only a single locking operation.

patches.name: 0436--NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-ttm-Avoid-evicting-unused-contiguous-buffers.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects:
[PATCH] [NOT-FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/ttm: Avoid evicting unused contiguous
 buffers
patches.rationale:
They're most likely going to be used for scanout and eventually moved
back. When they're moved back, stuff gets evicted at random until a long
enough contiguous memory range is found. This can frequently evict like
half of your VRAM, so if there's literally any way to not do that, try
taking that way.

However, if the buffers haven't been used for a really long time, assume
they're inert and try evicting them anyway. If something comes back and
uses them, the timeout is reset so the perf cliff should manifest as a
stutter on application switch at most.

patches.name: 0441--FOR-UPSTREAM-drm-amdgpu-Add-VRAM-claim-throttling.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FOR-UPSTREAM] drm/amdgpu: Add VRAM claim throttling
patches.rationale:
If someone else is trying to evict from a submitting process, things
can end up in rather nasty cycles of eviction, where A continuously
evicts from B, only for B to move everything back in at the cost of A's
memrory. Throttle claiming cgroup-protected memory to break such
pathological eviction loops.

Throttling happens per VM using two timeouts: "hard" throttling timeout
and "soft" throttling timeout. The idea is that once a VM notices a
different VM trying to evict its memory, it pulls the emergency stop and
only moves things into VRAM that are strictly necessary for
functionality. This avoids cycles where one VM constantly evicts a
buffer that another one moves back in. Progress will *eventually*
happen, but typically performance goes down the drain from this.

After the hard throttling timeout expires, we enter soft throttling
until its respective timeout expires. Under soft throttling, we're still
careful if any VM is still evicting from us, but we try claiming back
some VRAM that was stolen from us if it's free. If possible, we still
avoid evicting other apps, so that we don't go right back to square one.

Throttling is engaged when one of two conditions are met:
1. The VM is evicted from. In that case, assume the evicting VM might be
   even more hungry for memory. cgroup protection makes sure that the VM
   is only evicted from by VMs that are entitled to that memory, so
   there is no use in trying to fight it.
2. We tried evicting for our own buffers and failed. In this case, we
   reached a more or less steady state, and trying again is unlikely to
   change anything.

patches.name: 0443--FROM-ML-drm-amdgpu-Add-and-use-vm_update_ctx-struct.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-ML] drm/amdgpu: Add and use vm_update_ctx struct
patches.rationale:
This adds a "context" struct to the functions responsible for mapping
page tables (and committing the maps to the GPU page-tables).

The core idea here is to record the changes associated with specific VM
mapping operations (most importantly, which mappings were freed by each
map change). We need this to properly implement explicit sync for unmap
operations, which can only be performed for unmaps of either
always-valid or PRT mappings.

Before this patch, amdgpu_vm_clear_freed gets a list of pending unmap
operations with no insight where they come from - it's very much
possible that the list also contains unmap operations for which the sync
dependencies are unknown, and implicit sync semantics have to be
assumed.

By keeping a separate free-list in the context of each unmap operation
and only falling back to the global per-VM freelist if
amdgpu_vm_clear_freed can't be executed right now, we sidestep these
issues. We can also record information about sync dependencies (and
more, in subsequent patches) inside the context struct as well.

patches.name: 0444--FROM-ML-drm-amdgpu-Implement-explicit-sync-for-PRT-unmaps.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] [FROM-ML] drm/amdgpu: Implement explicit sync for PRT unmaps
patches.rationale:
In certain cases, it is possible to skip syncing with every submission
in the whole VM before unmapping pagetables. The important condition is
that no memory must be released to the system while the GPU still has a
chance to access it.

This is true for VM-always-valid buffers since the resv is shared with
the VM's root PD and thus there will always be synchronization before
unmapping, but also for PRT pages which do not point to any real memory
location at all. Bypass implicit sync for unmapping for these buffers if
userspace requests it. Userspace can request this via a new VM ioctl
flag.

patches.name: 0455-linux-integration-7.2.0-valve1.patch
patches.base_evidence: Parent commit of this downstream change in Valve's published Git history
patches.note: Individual downstream commit for inspection/cherry-picking; full series application is unverified.
subjects: [PATCH] linux-integration 7.2.0-valve1
patches.rationale:
TL;DR: Feature pairity with 6.18.46-valve1, plus updated xbox GIP
support. No known issues.

Changes since 7.2.0-rc3-valve-beta1:
- Rebase on 7.2
- HID: hid-msi: Update driver to version landed upstream
- Update Steam controller support to match what landed upstream
- Add HDMI VRR support
- Fix crash on MSI Claw devices that don't have any WMI quirk set
- Fix 5GHz connection instability on ath11k with APs reporting invalid
  MCS
- Fix power supply status wrongly reported as charging when connected to
  underpower power supply
- msi-wmi-platform: Enable TDP Support for MSI Claw A8 and 8 EX
- Update rtw89 backport to latest from rtw-next (until 38c58d541cfe)
- PCI + mmc: Fix hard-lock on resume from s2idle when SD/MMC
  card present on MSI Claw A8
- drm/amd/pm: Restore user-set GPU frequency after resume on AMD APUs
- drm/amd/display: Allow setting a floor for UCLK frequency to
  workaround HDA DMA dropouts
- drm/amdgpu: Disable runtime PM for externally attached dGPUs
- Various drm/amd fixes and improvements including drm_exec usage,
  cgroup throttling for memory eviction (except on APUs), and fixes for
  flip_done timedout events and GPU resets with VRR enabled
- drm/amdgpu: Reenable cgroup protection on APUs
- drm/amdgpu: Explicit sync for PRT unmaps
- drm/amdgpu: Use drm_exec in TTM and page table allocations
- input/xpad: Add support for Turtle Beach Xbox 360 controllers
- pinctrl-amd: Revert S4 wake bit clear omission that caused Steam
  Machine to immediately power back up after a power down
- Update xbox GIP support
